description: Prepare ONE visit of an upkeep you want done again and again at your own place, such as a weekly clean of your building. You pass your wallet, the upkeep's title, what needs doing, where, your own price, how many days apart the visits are (cadenceDays) and the day this visit is due (dueDate). The tool reads the jobs your wallet already posted. It allows one open visit of the same title at a time, and it says your wallet's day limit for free signed posts, with the time it opens again, before anything is signed. It writes the visit's paragraph and gives the visit its own key from the due date, so each visit is its own job. Returns MESSAGE_TO_SIGN and BODY_JSON; sign with your wallet's personal_sign, then call submit_post_work within 5 minutes. Nothing is scheduled: nothing posts a visit for you, so ask again when the next one is due. Nothing is paid by this tool. You are the poster of each visit: you set its price and you decide whether the work was done. Vealth is not a party to the job: it does not schedule your visits, it does not promise that a worker will come, and it does not decide the proof. Cost and signer: free, no gas; the person signs the result with their own wallet or passkey, and the house never holds a key.

cadenceDays.description: Days between visits, a whole number from 1 to 365. It is written into this visit's paragraph as 'every N days' and stored nowhere else.

creatorWallet.description: The 0x… address posting this work. It signs, and it owns the posting.

description.description: What needs doing, concretely: a stranger (or the poster themselves) should be able to do it from this text alone.

dueDate.description: The day this visit is due, as a calendar date YYYY-MM-DD. It becomes the visit's key, so posting the same dueDate again returns the same job. That holds only while the first one is still live.

expiresInDays.description: Days the packet stays open. Default is cadenceDays.

flags.description: Optional authority flags, the two the claim gate reads and no others: permit-required when the work needs a permit, regulated when it needs a licensed trade (licensed electrician, plumber or contractor, asbestos or lead abatement). The board records the need and keeps such work closed to claims while regulated claims are closed; never leave a flag off to make work claimable.

location.description: Where the work is: address or place name. Include GPS as 'lat,lng' in the text if you have it, because geolocated proof is checked against the packet's place.

proofRequirements.description: Optional. The proof items, one line each (at most 20, 600 characters each), e.g. 'photo of the tree beside a measuring stick'.

proofRule.description: What proof completes the work, e.g. 'GPS pin + photo of the tree next to a measuring stick + watering confirmation'.

proposedPayUsd.description: Proposed pay in USD. Proposed, not promised: unfunded packets settle as provable credit.

safetyNotes.description: Optional. The hazards and stop-work rules a worker must read before starting, at most 600 characters. A packet with safety notes asks every claimer to affirm they are 18 or over and have read this exact text.

skillLevel.description: Optional. Who can do this work: entry (a newcomer, safely, from the text alone), intermediate or advanced. Omitted, it posts as entry and the reply says so; the board's entry-level filter reads it, so never leave skilled work at the default.

standard.description: Optional. The documented standard this work serves (a snake_case id such as 'tree_planting_establishment'); when a refusal lists suggestedStandards, pass one of them here. Omit it and the board lands the title on a documented standard itself when the title is that work's name.

title.description: Short honest title, e.g. 'Monthly care and growth check, planted neem tree'.

workTypeLabel.description: Optional. A documented work type (snake_case) when you know the board's own name for the work.
